The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority has rescued 17 people after a Compressed Natural Gas-powered commercial bus caught fire following a reported gas explosion along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. One other passenger sustained severe burn injuries in the incident, which occurred at Berger Bus Stop on the Lagos-bound section of the expressway. The authority disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Director of Public Affairs and Enlightenment Department, Adebayo Taofiq. According to LASTMA, the bus, with registration number EKY 798 YK, was conveying 18 occupants, including the driver, from the Mowe-Ibafo axis towards Lagos when it reportedly caught fire. The statement read, “The unfortunate incident involved 18 occupants travelling from the Mowe-Ibafo axis towards Lagos when the fully loaded vehicle reportedly caught fire, triggering panic among passengers and other motorists plying the busy expressway. Personnel of the Ojodu Police Division provided security and maintained order at the scene during the rescue and firefighting operations. Commending the response, the General Manager of LASTMA, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, praised the authority’s personnel for their courage, operational dexterity and prompt intervention. Bakare-Oki said the incident underscored the importance of rapid emergency response, inter-agency collaboration and the deployment of adequately trained personnel in mitigating the consequences of road accidents. He urged commercial transport operators, particularly those using CNG-powered vehicles, to prioritise regular professional inspections, comply with prescribed safety standards and maintain their vehicles’ gas storage and delivery systems. The LASTMA general manager reiterated the authority’s commitment to protecting lives, ensuring smooth traffic movement and strengthening collaboration with emergency response agencies across Lagos State. He also commended the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Nigeria Police Force for their support during the operation.
